ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
n number of buttons are placed evenly around a circle. The buttons are labelled clockwise in order with the numbers 1 to $n$. The button with the number 7 is exactly opposite the button with the number 23. How big is $n$?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: n number of buttons are placed evenly around a circle. The buttons are labelled clockwise in order with the numbers 1 to $n$. The button with the number 7 is exactly opposite the button with the number 23. How big is $n$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a circle with button 7 near the upper-right side and button 23 near the lower-left side. A straight line connects 7 and 23 across the circle, matching the statement that they are opposite points. Reasoning: The buttons are labelled consecutively clockwise from 1 to n. Moving clockwise from button 7 to button 23 gives 23 - 7 = 16 label steps. Since button 7 is exactly opposite button 23, this distance is half the circle. Therefore half of the total number of buttons is 16, so n = 2 × 16 = 32.

method.method_draft: Use modular/cyclic-position reasoning. Read from the text that labels increase by 1 around a cycle of length n. If two labels are opposite, their positions differ by n/2 modulo n, so n must be even. The labels 7 and 23 differ by 23 - 7 = 16 positions in the clockwise numbering. Therefore n/2 = 16, giving n = 32.
